facts.statement: The genus Ramphastosula was described by Stucchi and Urbina in 2004.
Fossils of Ramphastosula date to the early Pliocene epoch.
The only named species, R. ramirezi, honors the Peruvian paleontologist Gregorio Ramirez.
facts.quote: The type and only named species is R. ramirezi, named for Peruvian vertebrate paleontologist Gregorio Ramirez.

facts.statement: The genus name combines the words for toucan and booby, with the latter derived from an Icelandic word meaning fool.
facts.quote: The genus name is a combination of "Rhamphastos", "toucan" and "sula", an Icelandic word for "fool" that has been used to describe boobies (Sulidae, Sula) in general.

facts.statement: Fossils were recovered from the 4 to 5 million-year-old Sud Sacaco Level of the Pisco Formation.
facts.quote: The remains were recovered from the west side of Sud Sacaco Level (4–5 Million year-old) of the Pisco Formation.

facts.statement: The habitat where the fossils were found was a sheltered beach featuring rock platforms.
facts.quote: This area was a sheltered beach with rock platforms.

facts.statement: Ramphastosula belongs to the bird family Sulidae.
The time range for Ramphastosula is estimated between 7.246 and 5.333 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Messinian to Messinian (7.246 to 5.333 million years ago)
